transcript.text: my belling cooker keeps burnin stuff 1 day then next day its undercookd on same temp. been like it a cuple months. thermastat??

It could be, but a thermostat is not the only likely cause. If the whole oven is sometimes too hot and sometimes too cool at the same setting, the temperature control is suspect — a dial-controlled oven may have a thermostat fault, while a display-controlled oven is more likely to have a sensor or control fault. If food is burning mainly on one side or on top while the rest is underdone, poor fan circulation, an element fault or a door-seal issue is more likely than the thermostat. Also check the same oven function is being used each time (not grill or rapid-heat), and remember fan-oven recipes normally need about 10–20°C less than conventional recipes. When it burns, is the whole dish cooking too fast, or is one side/top burning while another part stays undercooked?

its the whole thing really, not just one side. some days cakes go black at 180 and other days my lasagne is still cold in the middle after the usual time. only the main fan oven does it, top oven and grill are fine

That pattern is much more like the main oven is not regulating its temperature properly than a general cooking issue. Because the whole oven can be far too hot on one occasion and too cool on another, the leading cause is the temperature control: usually the oven thermostat if it has a numbered temperature dial, or the temperature sensor/control if it uses a digital display. An intermittent fan-oven element or connection is also possible, particularly for the cold-in-the-middle days, but would more often give consistently weak heating. Before using it again, just make sure the main oven is being set to the normal fan-oven symbol (fan with a ring around it), not defrost or a rapid-heat setting. Does the main oven temperature use a numbered dial, or a digital display/buttons?
its knobs, old fashioned ones with a neon light. no digital display or anything

With an old-style temperature knob, the main-oven thermostat is now the leading suspect. A thermostat that sticks or drifts can leave the oven heating for too long, so the whole dish cooks far too quickly; an intermittent fan-oven element or connection remains the other realistic cause for the weak/cold cooking days. On a day it is clearly getting too hot, does the main-oven neon stay on continuously, or does it switch on and off in cycles? If it stays lit while the oven is overheating, that points to the thermostat/control not cutting the heat off. Avoid relying on this oven for unattended cooking until it is sorted; thermostat or element work needs the cooker isolated and is normally an engineer job.
its a bit hard to say, sometimes the light goes off after about 10 mins but other times it seems to stay on for ages. is that the thermostat then?

Yes — the thermostat is the most likely cause, although the light alone does not prove it. It is normal for the neon to go out once temperature is reached and then come back on in cycles; however, it staying on for a long time on occasions when the oven then overheats fits a thermostat that is sticking or drifting. The cold/undercooked occasions leave an intermittent fan-oven element or connection as the next possibility, but that usually causes weak heating more consistently. Please just confirm the main oven is always being used on the normal fan-oven setting (fan inside a ring); if it is, this needs an engineer to test and likely check the thermostat or investigate the fan-oven heating circuit. Avoid unattended cooking with that oven meanwhile, as its temperature cannot be relied upon.

candidates: Oven thermostat or electronic temperature sensor/control not regulating accurately (medium)
Fan circulation or oven element fault causing uneven heat (medium)
Incorrect oven function, temperature setting or fan-oven recipe conversion (low)
